tool.name: PyEuk process-ONT
tool.description: call amplicon haplotypes from Oxford Nanopore reads, PyEuk process-ont
tool.command: pyeuk process-ont --input-fastq '$input_fastq' --sample-id '$sample_id' #if $reference_fasta --reference-fasta '$reference_fasta' #end if #if $de_novo --de-novo #end if --qscore $qscore --output-dir out && ## process-ont writes the calls to <output-dir>/<sample-id> (no extension). cp out/'$sample_id' '$calls'

param.name: sample_id
param.label: Sample identifier
param.help: Becomes the specimen id in the output.

param.name: reference_fasta
param.label: Reference MLST FASTA (optional)
param.help: Reference database of marker sequences. Omit and tick de novo to discover consensus haplotypes from the reads instead.

param.name: de_novo
param.label: De novo consensus discovery
param.help: Build consensus haplotypes from the reads without a reference database.

param.name: qscore
param.label: Minimum mean read Q-score
param.help: Reads below this mean quality are dropped before calling.

tool.help:
**Type an amplicon specimen from Oxford Nanopore reads**
Long ONT reads span a whole amplicon in one molecule, so a haplotype can be read off a single read. This tool quality-filters the reads, aligns them to the reference marker database (or builds a consensus **de novo** with no database), and writes per-specimen haplotype calls.
Give either a reference FASTA or tick **de novo**. Raise the **Q-score** floor to trade yield for accuracy on a noisy run. @HELP_FOOTER@
